criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a new test through Athena::go with an https github.com origin, a fake gh::Runner replying a green push run for the candidate SHA, and early_seam recording fakes shows the recording local check executor is never called, and the recorded check notes name CI as their source.
criteria.evidence: ci_reuse_green_skips_local_checks passed. It goes through ci_reuse_run, which installs early_seam, ci_seam (the CiReplies runner and a recording sleeper) and a recording check_seam, then calls Athena::go. The test asserts: executed is empty; the runs were read once; no sleep; every check note contains 'CI run <address> for <candidate>'; the job is Landed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a test with a red push run for the candidate SHA shows the job fails, the failure names the failing check, and no local check ran.
criteria.evidence: ci_reuse_red_fails_without_local_checks passed. It asserts: the state is Rejected; the only failed check is clippy; a checks line contains 'clippy FAILED'; done.reason contains 'clippy'; executed is empty; no sleep.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: tests with a missing run, a cancelled run and a timed-out run each show the local checks run as before and the job proceeds.
criteria.evidence: ci_reuse_falls_back_to_local_checks_when_the_run_gives_no_result passed. It covers four cases: Missing and Unfinished (76 reads, 75 pauses of 20 s on the fake sleeper) and Cancelled and TimedOut (1 read, no pause). In each case the executor ran fmt, clippy and test, and the job Landed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a test with no GitHub origin (none, or a local path) shows NoCi is used, the fake runner gets no call, and the wait does not apply (no sleeping, one read).

For each it asserts the runner recorded no paths, there were no sleeps, the local checks ran once each, and the job Landed. routing_no_wait_is_one_read_and_no_pause passed and shows one read with a zero bound and no pause for NoCi.

It asserts the captured verifier prompt contains verify::reuse_statement(&record, candidate), where candidate is the commit pushed to the CI branch. verification.rs pushes that statement as a 'ci-result' CheckResultView.

Athena::with_ci_source(job, wait_s, act) is defined once and returns either (NoCi, one read) or (Paced GitHub CI source, ci_polls(wait_s)). check_and_verify calls it with run_routed_with_record(&route, &c, ...), so the candidate commit c is the SHA passed to resolution.

findings.summary: The new https-only origin parser duplicates the one in gh/early.rs.
findings.evidence: Both bodies are identical except for how the separator character is written. Because early.rs was out of scope, the CI read and the CI-branch push now keep two copies of the 'is this a GitHub origin' rule, and the copies could drift apart. A later change should make early.rs call GhClient::origin_repository.

findings.summary: When the CI-branch push fails, the checks stage still waits out the full 1500 s bound before running the local checks.
findings.evidence: push_ci_branch only warns on failure, and with_ci_source does not know the push failed, so a missing run is polled 76 times. The CHANGELOG states this as a known cost. A simpler fix would be for push_ci_branch to return whether the push succeeded and to use NoCi when it did not.

summary: The change passes. With an https github.com origin, the checks stage now reads the push run on athena/ci/<job id> for the candidate commit. A green run skips the local checks and its result is reused. A red run fails the job and names clippy as the failing check. A missing, cancelled, timed-out or unfinished run falls back to the local checks. The wait is one read every 20 seconds, up to the new [budget] ci_wait_s = 1500. Any other origin, or a nested run, uses NoCi: one read, no wait, and no call to gh. When CI is green, the verifier's input gets the verify::reuse_statement text. I ran the five new ci_reuse tests through Athena::go, plus the routing and config tests, and all passed. git diff -G @ shows no added or removed line containing an at-sign; the client.rs code and its test write the userinfo separator as the escape '\u{40}'. Every changed file is on the deliverables list. test_support.rs and verify.rs were planned but left unchanged, which leaves no criterion unshown. There are two minor findings. A new https-only origin parser duplicates the one in gh/early.rs, which this job could not touch. A failed CI-branch push still waits out the full 1500 s bound before the local checks run; the CHANGELOG states this cost.
